prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

anchor.line: Believe you are free and you are. Believe you are bound and you are. As you think, so you become.

script: Your mind will not settle. You sit with the phone in your hand and the same thought looping. You feel scattered, and you do not know how to land anywhere.
Arjuna stands before Krishna on the battlefield. He has listened to Krishna speak of focus and action. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

Krishna does not argue. He agrees that it is difficult to master, but says that with repeated practice and the act of letting go, it can be trained. This is easier said than done, because you cannot force the mind to stop. You only give it a single place to rest, and let it go again. The texts call this the mind left to itself.
You do not need to fix the whole day right now. Pick one small thing to do with your hands. When the phone pulls you back, notice it, and let it go. One breath at a time.
What is the one thing your hands can do right now?

depth.life: You are sitting with the phone in your hand and the same thought looping. Your mind feels like it is running on a track it cannot get off. The texts call this the mind left to itself. It is not a flaw in you. It is a mind that has not been given a single place to rest.
depth.points: The mind is restless, turbulent and stubborn. It is like the wind. You cannot force it to stop. But you can train it. Practice and letting go are what shape it. The mind will not settle on its own.
depth.practice: Put the phone down for five minutes and watch your breath. Just notice it. Do not try to change it.
depth.question: What happens to your mind when you stop trying to hold it?
